event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: Digital Realty’s 2024 filing continues to frame COVID-19—and pandemics more broadly—as a live, but now moderating, threat.  Nearly four years have elapsed since the WHO declared COVID-19 a global pandemic, so the company’s language has shifted from emergency response to managing lingering impacts such as construction delays, labour availability, supply-chain bottlenecks, and potential customer defaults.  The risk discussion is still forward-looking ("may", "could", "cannot predict"), yet the narrative also cites concrete, already-experienced effects: project delays and economic volatility.  These disclosures remain mostly qualitative and unquantified, signalling uncertainty more than immediate balance-sheet damage.  Applying the Time-Decay Principle, the event now sits in the medium-term window (4-10 years).  Accordingly, evidence that refers to potential or ongoing impacts is scored in the mid-range (4-6).  Statements describing realised construction delays receive the higher end of that band, while generic cautionary language or sentences heavily tempered by mitigation measures score lower.  Mitigating statements (active supply-chain management, belief equipment will be delivered) are deducted in the micro-scorecards.  Overall, pandemic risk is still material but no longer acute; Digital Realty treats it as a persistent operational hazard rather than an existential threat.

evidence_list.snippet: Our business and operations, and our customers, suppliers and business partners may be adversely affected by epidemics, pandemics or other outbreaks.

components.reason: Explicitly links pandemics to adverse effects on the company’s ecosystem.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct statement of potential adverse impact; generic and unquantified, so mid-range score.

evidence_list.snippet: Epidemics, pandemics or other outbreaks of an illness, disease or virus that affect countries or regions in which we or our customers, suppliers or business partners operate, and actions taken to contain or prevent their further spread, may have a material and adverse impact on general commercial activity and on our financial condition, results of operations, liquidity and creditworthiness.

components.reason: States possibility of ‘material and adverse’ impact on multiple financial metrics.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Uses strong ‘material and adverse’ language across key financial areas, but forward-looking and unquantified.

evidence_list.snippet: Epidemics, pandemics or other outbreaks of an illness, disease or virus could result in significant governmental measures being implemented to control the spread of such illness, disease or virus, including quarantines, travel restrictions, manufacturing restrictions, declarations of states of emergency, business shutdowns, prioritization and allocation of resources, and restrictions on the movement of our employees and those of our customers, suppliers and business partners on which we rely, which could adversely affect our ability and their respective abilities to adequately manage our respective businesses.

components.reason: Details multiple disruptive government measures that could impair operations.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Enumerates concrete operational constraints; still conditional, hence moderate severity.

evidence_list.snippet: Risks related to epidemics, pandemics or other outbreaks of an illness, disease or virus could also lead to the complete or partial closure of one or more of our offices or properties or our customers’, suppliers’ or business partners’ businesses, or otherwise result in significant disruptions to our business and operations or theirs.

components.reason: Highlights potential property closures and ‘significant disruptions’.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specific operational threat (closures) but still phrased as potential; mid-range score.

evidence_list.snippet: Such events could materially and adversely impact our operations and the rental revenue we generate from our agreements with our customers or could result in defaults by our customers.

components.reason: Connects pandemics to lost rental revenue and customer defaults—direct financial exposure.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct linkage to revenue loss and credit risk raises severity within medium-term ceiling.

evidence_list.snippet: In particular, the global spread of COVID-19 and the various attempts to contain it have created significant volatility, uncertainty and economic disruption, including in construction activity.

components.reason: Describes realised ‘significant’ economic disruption tied to COVID-19.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Acknowledges past concrete disruption; time-decay caps score to upper-mid level.

evidence_list.snippet: We have experienced delays in construction activity in certain markets as a result of the availability of labor, and these delays have impacted and are continuing to impact some of our anticipated deliveries to our customers.

components.reason: Confirms actual ongoing construction delays affecting customer deliveries.
Time-decay adjustment (medium-term event, limits peak severity).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Concrete operational impact merits high points, reduced slightly for event age.

evidence_list.snippet: We may continue to experience delays in construction activity due to increased safety protocols implemented in response to the COVID-19 pandemic.

components.reason: Foresees future construction delays directly linked to pandemic protocols.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Forward-looking operational risk; moderately high severity.

evidence_list.snippet: We cannot predict the full extent of the impact that the epidemics, pandemics and other global events will have on our customers, suppliers and other business partners; however, any material effect on these parties could adversely impact us, our future financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.

components.reason: Admits uncertainty while warning of adverse financial effects.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Generic uncertainty language; lower mid-range score.

evidence_list.snippet: The full extent to which epidemics, pandemics and the various responses to such events impact our business, operations and financial results will depend on numerous evolving factors that we may not be able to accurately predict, including: the duration and scope of such event; governmental, business and individuals’ actions that have been and continue to be taken in response to such event; the availability of and cost to access the capital markets; the effect on our customers and customer demand for and ability to pay for our services; the impact on our development projects; and disruptions or restrictions on our employees’ ability to work and travel.

components.reason: Lists multiple financial and operational variables affected by pandemics.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Broad scenario planning without quantification; modest risk points.

evidence_list.snippet: During the pandemic and its related and other ongoing global supply chain issues, we have actively monitored our vendors and suppliers and remain in frequent communication with customers, contractors and suppliers.
evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Mentions risk but emphasises mitigation; net low score.

evidence_list.snippet: Although to date, we have been able to manage through disruptions in our supply chain and procurement process due to the pandemic and other global events, continuing disruptions could have a material adverse impact on our business and financial condition.

components.reason: States potential ‘material adverse’ impact from ongoing pandemic-related supply-chain disruptions.
Notes past successful management, partially mitigating future risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Acknowledges serious future risk but tempered by track record; moderate score.
